passages.text: Now we know that if the earthly tent we live in is dismantled, we have a building from God, an eternal house in heaven, not built by human hands.
passages.sermon:
We know something important.
We live now in an earthly tent.
This tent means our present, physical body.
If this earthly tent is destroyed, we do not lose hope.
God gives us something better.
God gives us a building from Him.
This building is an eternal house.
This house is in heaven.
Human hands did not build this house.
God made this house for us.
This house will last forever.
passages.original: Οἴδαμεν γὰρ ὅτι ἐὰν ἡ ἐπίγειος ἡμῶν οἰκία τοῦ σκήνους καταλυθῇ οἰκοδομὴν ἐκ Θεοῦ ἔχομεν οἰκίαν ἀχειροποίητον αἰώνιον ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς

passages.text: For in this tent we groan, longing to be clothed with our heavenly dwelling, because when we are clothed, we will not be found naked.
passages.sermon:
We live now in our earthly bodies.
We groan in these bodies.
We long for our heavenly home.
We desire to be clothed with our dwelling from heaven.
When God clothes us with this heavenly dwelling, we will not be found naked.
passages.original: καὶ γὰρ ἐν τούτῳ στενάζομεν τὸ οἰκητήριον ἡμῶν τὸ ἐξ οὐρανοῦ ἐπενδύσασθαι ἐπιποθοῦντες εἴ γε καὶ ἐνδυσάμενοι οὐ γυμνοὶ εὑρεθησόμεθα

passages.text: So while we are in this tent, we groan under our burdens, because we do not wish to be unclothed but clothed, so that our mortality may be swallowed up by life.
passages.sermon:
We live now in our earthly bodies.
We call these bodies our tents.
While we are in these bodies, we groan.
We feel heavy burdens.
We do not want to be without a body.
We want to be clothed with a new body.
We want life to swallow up our mortal bodies.
We long for our mortal life to be replaced by true life.
passages.original: καὶ γὰρ οἱ ὄντες ἐν τῷ σκήνει στενάζομεν βαρούμενοι ἐφ’ ᾧ οὐ θέλομεν ἐκδύσασθαι ἀλλ’ ἐπενδύσασθαι ἵνα καταποθῇ τὸ θνητὸν ὑπὸ τῆς ζωῆς

passages.text: And God has prepared us for this very purpose and has given us the Spirit as a pledge of what is to come.
passages.sermon: God has prepared us for this purpose.\r\nGod has given us the Holy Spirit.\r\nThe Holy Spirit is a pledge of what is to come.
passages.original: ὁ δὲ κατεργασάμενος ἡμᾶς εἰς αὐτὸ τοῦτο Θεός ὁ δοὺς ἡμῖν τὸν ἀρραβῶνα τοῦ Πνεύματος

passages.text: Therefore we are always confident, although we know that while we are at home in the body, we are away from the Lord.
passages.sermon:
We are followers of Christ.
We are always confident.
We know something important.
When we live in this body, we are away from the Lord.
passages.original: Θαρροῦντες οὖν πάντοτε καὶ εἰδότες ὅτι ἐνδημοῦντες ἐν τῷ σώματι ἐκδημοῦμεν ἀπὸ τοῦ Κυρίου

passages.text: For we walk by faith, not by sight.
passages.sermon: We live by faith.\r\nWe do not live by what we see.
passages.original: διὰ πίστεως γὰρ περιπατοῦμεν οὐ διὰ εἴδους

passages.text: We are confident, then, and would prefer to be away from the body and at home with the Lord.
passages.sermon:
Paul is a Christian apostle.
Paul and his companions feel confident.
They would rather leave their bodies.
They would rather be at home with the Lord.
passages.original: Θαρροῦμεν δὲ καὶ εὐδοκοῦμεν μᾶλλον ἐκδημῆσαι ἐκ τοῦ σώματος καὶ ἐνδημῆσαι πρὸς τὸν Κύριον

passages.text: So we aspire to please Him, whether we are here in this body or away from it.
passages.sermon:
We want to please the Lord.
We make this our goal.
We try to please Him at all times.
We do this whether we live in our bodies or are away from them.
We do this because we belong to the Lord.
passages.original: διὸ καὶ φιλοτιμούμεθα εἴτε ἐνδημοῦντες εἴτε ἐκδημοῦντες εὐάρεστοι αὐτῷ εἶναι

passages.text: For we must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ, that each one may receive his due for the things done in the body, whether good or bad.
passages.sermon:
All people must stand before Christ.
Christ will judge every person.
Each person will receive what is due for what they have done in their body.
Each deed will be judged.
Good deeds and bad deeds will both be judged.
passages.original: τοὺς γὰρ πάντας ἡμᾶς φανερωθῆναι δεῖ ἔμπροσθεν τοῦ βήματος τοῦ Χριστοῦ ἵνα κομίσηται ἕκαστος τὰ διὰ τοῦ σώματος πρὸς ἃ ἔπραξεν εἴτε ἀγαθὸν εἴτε φαῦλον

passages.text: Therefore, since we know what it means to fear the Lord, we try to persuade men. What we are is clear to God, and I hope it is clear to your conscience as well.
passages.sermon:
We know what it means to fear the Lord.
We try to persuade people.
God sees who we truly are.
I hope you also see who we are in your conscience.
passages.original: Εἰδότες οὖν τὸν φόβον τοῦ Κυρίου ἀνθρώπους πείθομεν Θεῷ δὲ πεφανερώμεθα ἐλπίζω δὲ καὶ ἐν ταῖς συνειδήσεσιν ὑμῶν πεφανερῶσθαι

passages.text: We are not commending ourselves to you again. Instead, we are giving you an occasion to be proud of us, so that you can answer those who take pride in appearances rather than in the heart.
passages.sermon:
We are not commending ourselves to you again.
We are giving you an occasion to be proud of us.
You can answer those who take pride in appearances.
They do not take pride in the heart.
passages.original: οὐ πάλιν ἑαυτοὺς συνιστάνομεν ὑμῖν ἀλλὰ ἀφορμὴν διδόντες ὑμῖν καυχήματος ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν ἵνα ἔχητε πρὸς τοὺς ἐν προσώπῳ καυχωμένους καὶ μὴ ἐν καρδίᾳ

passages.text: If we are out of our mind, it is for God; if we are of sound mind, it is for you.
passages.sermon:
Paul is an apostle of Jesus Christ.
\r\nPaul sometimes acts in ways that seem unusual or extreme.
\r\nIf Paul seems out of his mind, he does this for God.
\r\nIf Paul is in his right mind, he does this for the people he serves.
passages.original: Εἴτε γὰρ ἐξέστημεν Θεῷ εἴτε σωφρονοῦμεν ὑμῖν

passages.text: For Christ’s love compels us, because we are convinced that One died for all, therefore all died.
passages.sermon:
Christ loves us.
His love compels us.
We are convinced of something important.
One person died for everyone.
Because One died for all, all died.
passages.original: ἡ γὰρ ἀγάπη τοῦ Χριστοῦ συνέχει ἡμᾶς κρίναντας τοῦτο ὅτι εἷς ὑπὲρ πάντων ἀπέθανεν ἄρα οἱ πάντες ἀπέθανον

passages.text: And He died for all, that those who live should no longer live for themselves, but for Him who died for them and was raised again.
passages.sermon:
Jesus Christ died for all people.
He died so that those who live should not live for themselves.
They should live for Jesus Christ.
Jesus Christ died for them.
God raised Jesus Christ from the dead.
passages.original: καὶ ὑπὲρ πάντων ἀπέθανεν ἵνα οἱ ζῶντες μηκέτι ἑαυτοῖς ζῶσιν ἀλλὰ τῷ ὑπὲρ αὐτῶν ἀποθανόντι καὶ ἐγερθέντι

passages.text: So from now on we regard no one according to the flesh. Although we once regarded Christ in this way, we do so no longer.
passages.sermon:
We are followers of Christ.
From now on, we do not judge anyone by human standards.
In the past, we saw Christ in a human way.
Now, we do not see Christ in that way anymore.
passages.original: Ὥστε ἡμεῖς ἀπὸ τοῦ νῦν οὐδένα οἴδαμεν κατὰ σάρκα εἰ καὶ ἐγνώκαμεν κατὰ σάρκα Χριστόν ἀλλὰ νῦν οὐκέτι γινώσκομεν

passages.text: Therefore if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation. The old has passed away. Behold, the new has come!
passages.sermon:
Anyone who is in Christ is a new creation.
Christ is the Son of God.
God sent Christ to save us.
The old things have passed away.
The new things have come.
passages.original: ὥστε εἴ τις ἐν Χριστῷ καινὴ κτίσις τὰ ἀρχαῖα παρῆλθεν ἰδοὺ γέγονεν καινά

passages.text: All this is from God, who reconciled us to Himself through Christ and gave us the ministry of reconciliation: that God was reconciling the world to Himself in Christ, not counting men’s trespasses against them. And He has committed to us the message of reconciliation.
passages.sermon:
God is the source of everything.
God reconciled us to Himself through Christ.
God gave us the ministry of reconciliation.
God was in Christ.
God was reconciling the world to Himself in Christ.
God did not count people’s trespasses against them.
God entrusted to us the message of reconciliation.
passages.original: Τὰ δὲ πάντα ἐκ τοῦ Θεοῦ τοῦ καταλλάξαντος ἡμᾶς ἑαυτῷ διὰ Χριστοῦ καὶ δόντος ἡμῖν τὴν διακονίαν τῆς καταλλαγῆς ὡς ὅτι Θεὸς ἦν ἐν Χριστῷ κόσμον καταλλάσσων ἑαυτῷ μὴ λογιζόμενος αὐτοῖς τὰ παραπτώματα αὐτῶν καὶ θέμενος ἐν ἡμῖν τὸν λόγον τῆς καταλλαγῆς

passages.text: Therefore we are ambassadors for Christ, as though God were making His appeal through us. We implore you on behalf of Christ: Be reconciled to God.
passages.sermon:
We represent Christ.
We serve as ambassadors for Him.
God makes His appeal through us.
We urge you for Christ’s sake.
Be reconciled to God.
passages.original: Ὑπὲρ Χριστοῦ οὖν πρεσβεύομεν ὡς τοῦ Θεοῦ παρακαλοῦντος δι’ ἡμῶν δεόμεθα ὑπὲρ Χριστοῦ καταλλάγητε τῷ Θεῷ

passages.text: God made Him who knew no sin to be sin on our behalf, so that in Him we might become the righteousness of God.
passages.sermon:
God acted.
God made Jesus to be sin for us.
Jesus had never known sin.
God did this for our sake.
God wanted us to become righteous in Jesus.
God wanted us to have His righteousness through Jesus.
passages.original: τὸν μὴ γνόντα ἁμαρτίαν ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν ἁμαρτίαν ἐποίησεν ἵνα ἡμεῖς γενώμεθα δικαιοσύνη Θεοῦ ἐν αὐτῷ
